newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan subway guru heckles court as trial resumes.
newsitem.headline: Japan subway guru heckles court as trial resumes.

text.p: Doomsday cult guru Shoko Asahara, accused of masterminding the Tokyo subway nerve gas attack, kept up his courtroom heckling when his trial resumed on Thursday at the Tokyo District Court after a one-month break.
Asahara, in a blue and white tracksuit, sat restlessly in his seat and constantly fiddled with his beard and hair during the day-long session.
"Stop this silly trial," "What are you saying?" "Don't ask such questions," Asahara said loudly, prompting the judge to warn him several times to keep quiet.
The partially sighted guru has refused to enter a plea and has several times disrupted his twice-monthly trial sessions with loud outbursts that have twice led him to be evicted from the courtroom.

On the witness stand on Thursday was Yoshihiro Inoue, one of the key members of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect), which is accused of releasing sarin nerve gas in Tokyo subways in March 1995, killing 12 people and injuring thousands.
Asahara's lawyers grilled Inoue on minute details of events leading to the attack in what appeared an apparent effort to discredit testimony by the cult's former intelligence chief.
Inoue is also on trial for his part in the gas attack.
During the cross examination, Inoue denied having been informed by a former police officer and cult member about police plans to raid the cult's compound.
"I did not receive information on a (planned) police raid," Inoue said.
The former officer, Toshiyuki Kosugi, has confessed to being involved in the shooting of National Police Agency (NPA) chief Takaji Kunimatsu shortly after the subway attack.
Apart from the subway murder charges, Asahara faces 16 other charges ranging from kidnapping to illegal production of drugs and weapons.
